newer.quote: Cursor values are URL-safe strings that are opaque to the client.

target.quote: Table 6 describes the URL pagination parameters.
target.subject: cursor query parameter

amendments.effect: Servers and clients may use a new "cursor" query parameter for cursor-based pagination alongside startIndex and count.

newer.quote: the response includes the optional previousCursor indicating that the service provider supports forward and reverse traversal of result pages.

target.quote: The following attributes are defined for responses:
target.subject: nextCursor, previousCursor ListResponse attributes

amendments.effect: ListResponse gains the nextCursor and previousCursor attributes; nextCursor MUST be present on every page except the last when cursor pagination is supported.

newer.quote: Service providers implementing cursor pagination that are unable to estimate totalResults MAY choose to omit the totalResults attribute.

target.quote: totalResults  The total number of results returned by the list or query operation.
target.subject: totalResults

amendments.condition: when cursor-based pagination is used and the service provider cannot estimate the total
amendments.effect: totalResults, REQUIRED in a ListResponse, may be omitted in cursor-paginated responses when the provider cannot estimate it.

newer.quote: These error types extend the list defined in Table 9 ("SCIM Detail Error Keyword Values") of Section 3.12 of [RFC7644]

target.quote: Table 9: SCIM Detail Error Keyword Values
target.subject: scimType detail error keywords

amendments.effect: Three new scimType values (invalidCursor, expiredCursor, invalidCount) are added for 400 responses to GET queries.

newer.quote: When posting to /.search, the client would pass the parameters defined in Section 2 in the body of the POST request.

target.quote: Clients MAY execute queries without passing parameters on the URL by using the HTTP POST verb combined with the "/.search" path extension.
target.subject: POST /.search search request parameters

amendments.effect: The "cursor" parameter (and count) may also be sent in the JSON body of a POST /.search request.

newer.quote: A SCIM service provider implementing cursor-based pagination SHOULD include the following additional attribute in a JSON document returned by the /ServiceProviderConfig endpoint:

target.quote: The following singular attributes are defined in addition to the common attributes defined in the core schema:
target.subject: ServiceProviderConfig pagination attribute

amendments.effect: ServiceProviderConfig gains an OPTIONAL complex "pagination" attribute (cursor, index, defaultPaginationMethod, defaultPageSize, maxPageSize, cursorTimeout) that providers SHOULD publish when supporting cursors.

newer.quote: Section 2 of this document has been added to the References column.

target.quote: As per the "SCIM Schema URIs for Data Resources" registry established by [RFC7643]
target.subject: IANA schema URI registry references

amendments.effect: IANA registry entries for ListResponse, SearchRequest and ServiceProviderConfig now also reference RFC 9865.

newer.quote: This section defines additional attributes that enable a SCIM client to discover the additional capabilities defined by this specification.

target.quote: The following singular attributes are defined in addition to the common attributes defined in the core schema:
target.subject: ServiceProviderConfig securityEvents attribute

amendments.effect: ServiceProviderConfig gains an OPTIONAL "securityEvents" complex attribute (asyncRequest, eventUris) advertising async and Security Event support.

newer.quote: A SCIM client making SCIM HTTP requests defined in Section 3 of [RFC7644] MAY request asynchronous processing using the "Prefer" HTTP header

target.quote: SCIM is a protocol that is based on HTTP [RFC7230].
target.subject: asynchronous SCIM requests (Prefer: respond-async)

amendments.effect: Clients may send POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE with "Prefer: respond-async"; providers may answer 202 with Set-Txn and later deliver a completion event.

newer.quote: When an asynchronous response is requested, a single Asynchronous Request Completion Event MUST be generated for each requested operation.

target.quote: The SCIM bulk operation is an optional server feature that enables clients to send a potentially large collection of resource operations in a single request.
target.subject: asynchronous bulk requests

amendments.effect: When a bulk request is processed asynchronously, one completion event per bulk operation is generated, possibly out of order but with txn numbers matching request order.

newer.quote: A reference to Section 4 of this document has been added to the "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:ServiceProviderConfig" entry

target.quote: The IANA has populated the "System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) Schema URIs" registry
target.subject: IANA SCIM Server-Related Schema URIs registry

amendments.effect: The ServiceProviderConfig registry entry now also references RFC 9967 Section 4.

newer.quote: IANA has created a new registry called "SCIM Event URIs" under the "System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) Schema URIs" registry group

target.quote: To manage this sub-namespace, IANA has created the "System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) Schema URIs" registry
target.subject: IANA SCIM registry group

amendments.effect: A new "SCIM Event URIs" registry (Expert Review) exists under the SCIM registry group.

newer.quote: If sorting is implemented as described Section 3.4.2.3 of [RFC7644], then cursor-paged results should be sorted.

target.quote: Sorting allows clients to specify the order in which resources are returned by specifying a combination of "sortBy" and "sortOrder" URL parameters.
target.subject: sorting cursor-paged results

amendments.condition: when both cursor-based pagination and sorting are supported
amendments.effect: When sorting is implemented per Section 3.4.2.3, cursor-paged queries deliver results in the requested sort order across cursor pages.
